notes.meaning: God speaks directly to Ezekiel to give him a new prophecy. This message looks ahead to a time when God's people have returned to their homeland. God warns them ahead of time about future enemies so they will trust Him when trouble comes.

God commands Ezekiel to speak against Gog, a powerful ruler over the land of Magog and territories to the far north. God announces that He is an enemy to this proud leader. No matter how strong an earthly king may be, God remains the supreme ruler over all nations.

differ.view: Some see Gog as a future political and military leader who will head a literal northern alliance against Israel in the end times.
Many see Gog not as one specific individual, but as a symbolic figure representing the gathered enemies of God's people throughout history.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic interpreters often view Gog as a general figure for persecutors of the church, especially the Antichrist, though some historically connect the name with King Gyges of Lydia.

notes.meaning: God pictures Gog as a stubborn wild beast that He will drag wherever He wants. He puts hooks in Gog's mouth to pull his massive army out to battle with all their horses and weapons. Even though the enemy thinks he is choosing his own path, God is completely directing events to bring about his defeat.

A large alliance from distant lands joins Gog's northern forces. These armies come from Persia to the east, Cush and Put to the south in Africa, and Gomer and Beth-togarmah from the north. They arrive fully armed and ready to attack God's people together.

God ironically tells Gog to make ready all his troops and weapons. Gog is commanded to take charge and guard the massive coalition he has gathered. Yet all this military preparation will be useless against God's power.

Long after Ezekiel's lifetime, Gog will be summoned to march against the land of Israel. The Jewish people have been brought back home from many nations after long years of war and ruin. Attacking people who have just begun to live in peaceful security shows how cruel this invader is.

Gog and his allied armies will advance suddenly like a violent storm. His troops are so vast that they will cover the land like a giant dark cloud. Their terrifying numbers seem impossible for any human force to stop.

God describes the evil thoughts that will enter Gog's mind at that time. Even though God guides events, Gog acts out of his own wicked heart and free choice. Great acts of cruelty begin with selfish thoughts.

Gog decides to attack because the towns in Israel have no defensive walls, gates, or bars. He sees a quiet, defenseless people living at the center of the land with growing wealth, cattle, and goods. Greed drives him to rob and plunder those who suspect no harm.

Trading nations from Arabia and distant coastlines notice Gog's huge march. Instead of stopping the violence, they ask if they can buy and trade the stolen goods. They are eager to profit from the suffering and robbery of others.

God tells Ezekiel to announce that Gog will strike when Israel is living peacefully and safely. Gog will bring his vast cavalry from the far north like a cloud over the land. Yet God is drawing him there so that when He destroys Gog, all nations will witness God's holy power.

God asks Gog if he is the very enemy foretold long ago by the earlier prophets of Israel. Those prophets had spoken for years about a final gathering of nations against God's people. God's ancient warnings and plans never fail to happen.

The moment Gog sets foot on Israel's soil, God's burning anger blazes up against him. A massive earthquake will rock the land so violently that fish, birds, beasts, and all people will tremble. Mountains will tumble down, rocky cliffs will crumble, and defensive walls will fall flat.

God calls for a sword of judgment across all the hills of Israel. Panic and sheer confusion will strike Gog's diverse army so deeply that the soldiers will begin fighting each other. God easily turns the weapons of the wicked against their own allies.

God finishes Gog's army with deadly plagues and terrible bloodshed. He pours out flooding rains, giant hailstones, fire, and burning sulfur, just as He did long ago on Sodom. Nature itself fights under God's command to wipe out the invaders.

Through this awesome victory, God shows that He is entirely holy, powerful, and faithful to His word. Many nations will watch this deliverance and finally realize that He alone is the true Lord. God's ultimate goal in history is that all people recognize His glory.
